'''Ryōhei Mori''' (森 良平, born November 1973) is a Japanese scientist, inventor, and entrepreneur. He is the CEO of Green Science Alliance Co., Ltd. and Fuji Pigment Co., Ltd., and serves as President of Quantum Materials Technology and e-Gle Tech Co., Ltd. Mori is known for his work in eco-friendly green technologies, including aluminium-based rechargeable batteries, recycled lithium-ion batteries derived from black mass, carbon dioxide (CO₂) conversion methods, quantum dots, metal–organic frameworks, deep eutectic solvents, solid acid catalysts, and petroleum-free biodegradable plastics and plant biomass-based materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Member Spotlight – Ryohei Mori |url=https://www.electrochem.org/ecsnews/member-spotlight-ryohei-mori/ |website=Electrochemical Society |date=13 January 2015 |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref>

== Education ==
Mori earned his undergraduate degree in Applied Biology from Kyoto Institute of Technology in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corporate Profile – Fuji Pigment Co., Ltd. |url=http://www.fuji-pigment.co.jp/en/company/profile_en.html |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref> He received his M.Sc. (1999) and Ph.D. in engineering (2005) from [[Kyoto University]]. In 2021, he completed the General Management Program at [[Harvard Business School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Venture Competition 2022: Business and Environment Ventures |url=https://www.hbs.edu/environment/blog/post/NVC2022 |website=Harvard Business School |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=10 January 2024 |title=Ryohei Mori: Pioneering Green Technology for a Sustainable Future |url=https://thebusinessfame.com/ryohei-mori-pioneering-green-technology-for-a-sustainable-future/ |website=The Business Fame |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2023-03-09 |title=Replacing all petroleum-based chemical products with natural biomass-based chemical products: a tutorial review |journal=RSC Sustainability |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=179–212 |doi=10.1039/D2SU00014H |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Career ==
Mori joined Fuji Pigment Co., Ltd., where he later became CEO. In 2010, he established Green Science Alliance Co., Ltd. He has developed and commercialized rechargeable aluminium-based battery systems designed for safer and more sustainable energy storage, including aqueous aluminium-ion batteries and recycled lithium-ion batteries produced from black mass.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2017 |title=Suppression of byproduct accumulation in rechargeable aluminum–air batteries using non-oxide ceramic materials as air cathode materials |journal=Sustainable Energy & Fuels |volume=1 |issue=5 |pages=1082–1089 |doi=10.1039/C7SE00087A |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Ryohei Mori |url=https://acs.digitellinc.com/b/sp/ryohei-mori-315786 |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2017 |title=Rechargeable aluminum–air battery using deep eutectic solvent electrolyte |journal=RSC Advances |volume=7 |issue= |pages= |doi=10.1039/C6RA25164A|doi-access=free }}</ref>

He is also known for creating fully biodegradable plastics and a wide range of bio-based materials derived from natural plant biomass without using petroleum-based components.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bio-beauty: world's first plant-based biodegradable nail tips |url=https://worldbiomarketinsights.com/bio-beauty-worlds-first-plant-based-biodegradable-nail-tips/ |date=27 July 2023 |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Realization of a Global Green Future |url=https://www.theworldfolio.com/interviews/the-realization-of-global-green-future/6478/ |website=The Worldfolio |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref>

In 2023, his work on plant- and biomass-based biochemical materials was featured on the cover of ''RSC Sustainability''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2023 |title=Replacing all petroleum-based chemical products with natural biomass-based chemical products |journal=RSC Sustainability |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=179–212 |doi=10.1039/D2SU00014H|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2025, his work on aqueous aluminium-ion batteries was featured on the cover of ''Energy Advances''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2025 |title=Aqueous aluminium-ion battery for sustainable energy storage |journal=Energy Advances |doi=10.1039/D5YA00148J|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Green Science Alliance Co., Ltd. is supported by United Nations organizations. The company was selected as a green technology startup supported by the incubation programme of UNOPS GIC Japan in 2020, and their green technologies are registered at [[WIPO GREEN]]. In 2025, the company acquired grant funding for a green industrial recovery project for Ukraine from UNIDO.

Dr. Mori participated as a speaker at the United Nations Pavilion at [[Expo 2025|EXPO 2025]] Osaka, Japan, in October 2025 to showcase WIPO GREEN's role in providing sustainable solutions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WIPO GREEN News |url=https://www3.wipo.int/wipogreen/en/news/2025/news_0011.html |website=WIPO GREEN |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref> He was featured in ''Newsweek International'' magazine to promote sustainable innovation in July 2025, and was also described as one of the [[startup company]] CEOs showcasing at EXPO 2025 Osaka in ''Time Magazine'' in April 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robotics & Recycling: Japan Leads the Next Manufacturing Era |url=https://d.newsweek.com/en/file/478244/robotics-recycling-japan-leads-next-manufacturing-era.pdf |website=Newsweek |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=EXPO 2025 Showcases the Best in Business |url=https://partners.time.com/partners/global-kigyo/expo-2025-showcases-the-best-in-business/ |website=Time |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref>

== Research focus ==
Mori’s research focuses on sustainable technologies in energy and materials science.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mori |first=Ryohei |date=2024-04-01 |title=CO2 photocatalytic reduction with robust and stable metal–organic framework: a review |journal=Materials for Renewable and Sustainable Energy |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=109–132 |doi=10.1007/s40243-023-00252-5|doi-access=free }}</ref> His work includes rechargeable aluminium-based batteries, recycled lithium-ion batteries from black mass, and carbon dioxide conversion technologies.

He has also developed biodegradable polymers and chemicals derived from natural biomass to replace petroleum-based plastics.

Furthermore, Mori has been involved in the development of quantum dot applications. Specifically, he has developed quantum dots made from various types of waste, such as organic biomass waste, plastic waste, food waste, household garbage, and solid municipal waste, which can be applied to fertilizers, antimicrobial materials, pesticides, and insect repellents.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Japanese Firm Unveils World's First Quantum Dot Nail Polish Products |url=https://quantumzeitgeist.com/japanese-firm-unveils-worlds-first-quantum-dot-nail-polish-products/ |date=23 September 2024 |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref> He is also intensively researching metal–organic frameworks, deep eutectic solvents, solid acid catalysts, platinum-free (or reduced) fuel cells, perovskite solar cells, and organic thin-film solar cells.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Science Alliance succeeded in quantum dot–MOF composite material |url=https://www.photonicsonline.com/doc/green-science-alliance-succeeded-in-quantum-dot-mof-composite-material-0001 |website=Photonics Online |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fuji Pigment Develops Metal-Free QD Manufacturing Process |url=https://www.photonics.com/Articles/Fuji_Pigment_Develops_Metal-Free_QD_Manufacturing/a60614 |website=Photonics.com |access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref>
